text:
zoe: Noticing a warmstart OOM spike for mariner11b-int4 on canary pool after the traffic ramp.
zoe: Sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-23T09:07:11Z] OOM allocating 1.05GiB for kv_cache shard 2
model=mariner11b-int4 host=canary-hp-3 slot=2 prefetch=9 max_new_tokens=720
trace: kv_cache.rehydrate -> slab.alloc -> memset -> OOM
```
hassan: Looks similar to other models we've seen KV rehydration + high prefetch -> frag. What are current defaults in the model catalog?
zoe: defaults: prefetch=9, max_new_tokens=720, max_batch=8, soft_reserve=false.
ryan: quick mitigations we should try in canary: drop prefetch to 2, set max_new_tokens to 256, enable soft_reserve and slab_compact_on_evict. Also try microbatching to reduce simultaneous KV growth.
clem: i'll run a short local runner sim with mixed-length sessions (short prompts, multi-turn history) and check peak kv_alloc and slab_frag.

clem: local sim results: prefetch=2 + max_new_tokens=256 + microbatch=4 -> peak kv_alloc down ~58%, slab_frag_ratio down 22pp. latency p95 improved slightly for short sessions, but long-rollup tests (>2500 tokens) show more chunked generation.
hassan: tradeoff expected. For long-rollup traffic we can route to a highmem pool or keep a highmem model variant with larger defaults.
zoe: i've prepared a minimalist patch to model defaults for canaries:
```
model_defaults:
  max_new_tokens: "256"
  prefetch: "2"
  max_batch_size: "4"
  soft_reserve: "true"
  slab_compact_on_evict: "true"
```
ops-bot: deploybot: Rolling update 6210001234 -> mariner11b-int4 canary defaults patch started. dashboard: https://console.redwood/models/mariner11b/canaries/6210001234
ryan: baseline A/B (30m) after rolling to 2/3 canaries: OOM rate v1=12.4% -> v2=0.8%. p95 latency v1=125ms -> v2=96ms. cost/request approx -3.6%.
clem: quality quickcheck on our 600 prompt set: no statistically significant regressions for prompts <2k tokens. For the 120 long-rollup prompts >2k tokens, we see length truncation and slightly lower Rouge-L on a few examples.
hassan: we'll run a targeted eval against the long-rollup suite and also sanity-check hallucination rates. If regression is only when hitting the new max_new_tokens cap, we should implement policy: route requests with client max_tokens+history_estimate>2k to highmem or set per-route override.
zoe: created ticket INFRA-3501 for routing rule + metrics and PR #902 for defaults change. Linking tests results: https://ci.redwood/builds/902/artifacts/long_rollup_eval
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary v2 succeeded on 3/3 hosts. Monitoring window: 24h.
ryan: follow-ups: add runtime gauges: kv_alloc_peak, slab_frag_ratio, active_prefetch_windows. Alert if kv_alloc_peak > 900MiB or slab_frag_ratio > 30% on mariner11b hosts.
clem: will also add a quick trace to log kv_rebuild_latency to see if compaction adds CPU overhead.
zoe: plan: keep patch in canary 24h, run long-rollup eval + hallucination checks. If OOM <1% and long-rollup quality regression <= 1% absolute, promote to dedicated canaries.
hassan: if long-rollup quality fails, fallback option: maintain two variants in catalog (mariner11b-optimized and mariner11b-highmem) and auto-route by length.
zoe: thanks all, updating INFRA-3501 and will post results here. :thumbsup:
